Make a product grant exactly these perks, adding and removing what differs. Without perks it asks in
a terminal; --none grants none.

Removing a perk asks first, since people who bought the product lose it; --yes skips that. Running
it again finishes a change that failed halfway.

Usage:
  voidhash product perks set [product] [perk...] [flags]

Arguments:
  product  The product's slug, name or id
  perk     Every perk the product should grant: its slug, name or id

Flags:
      --dry-run            Show what would change, and change nothing
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --json               Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --none               Grant no perks at all
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet              Print only ids, one per line
  -y, --yes                Make the change without asking for confirmation

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash product perks set pro-monthly premium ad-free
  voidhash product perks set pro-monthly premium --dry-run
  voidhash product perks set lifetime --none --yes
